newsitem.title: JAPAN: April long-term prime seen flat despite JGB rally.
newsitem.headline: April long-term prime seen flat despite JGB rally.

text.p: Japan's long-term prime lending rate for April is likely to be set at 2.5 percent next week, unchanged from the previous month, officials at long-term credit banks said on Friday.

The prime rate is unlikely to reflect the recent declines in yields on Japanese government bonds (JGBs) because long-term credit banks' debentures, on which the prime rate is based, have failed to follow the JGB rally, they said.
The yield of the key 182nd 10-year JGB hit a record low for any benchmark JGB of 2.120 percent on Friday. The yield was about 2.4 percent a month ago.
The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) is expected to announce its long-term prime rate for April next Tuesday.

The prime rate, at which long-term credit banks lend to their most creditworthy customers, is customarily set 0.9 percentage point above the coupon rate of benchmark IBJ five-year debentures issued monthly.
The IBJ's March five-year bank debenture, with a coupon rate of 1.6 percent, was traded at a yield of 1.63 percent on Friday, traders said.
Judging from current market conditions, the long-term prime rate is likely to be left unchanged in April, they said.
Investors now prefer JGBs over bank debentures, which have more credit risk and are less liquid than government bonds, traders said.
"Behind the current JGB rally is safe-haven buying by local investors fleeing riskier yen bonds such as bank debentures," said a senior dealer at a "Big Four" brokerage.
The yield on Nippon Credit Bank Ltd's (NCB) debentures, for example, remained high even after the bank on Tuesday announced restructuring measures aimed at restoring its financial health.
The 4.8 percent NCB five-year debenture due in September was traded at a yield of 5.8 percent on Friday, traders said. The yield rose as high as 8.0 percent on March 27.
